root_cause.text: The ib_uverbs_post_send function in the RDMA/uverbs subsystem allocates memory using an unvalidated user-provided wqe_size without ensuring it meets the minimum size of struct ib_uverbs_send_wr, resulting in out-of-bounds reads when accessing structure fields.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "ib_uverbs_post_send() uses cmd.wqe_size from userspace without any validation before passing it to kmalloc()", and the patch adds the guard "if (cmd.wqe_size < sizeof(struct ib_uverbs_send_wr))" immediately before the allocation call to enforce the minimum size requirement.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the unvalidated user-provided cmd.wqe_size to calculate memory offsets via size_mul() before any minimum size validation check. The vulnerability root cause indicates that wqe_size must meet the minimum size of struct ib_uverbs_send_wr, but this call happens BEFORE the validation check at lines 2052-2053. This creates a TOCTOU race condition where out-of-bounds access can occur when uverbs_request_next_ptr returns pointers based on the unvalidated size, allowing attackers to trigger OOB reads when accessing structure fields.
